questions.prompt: At a straight two-link arm, a rank-deficient endpoint Jacobian means…
options: Some instantaneous endpoint directions are unavailable.
Forward kinematics cannot be computed for that pose.
questions.explanation: Rank loss restricts instantaneous task motion; joint coordinates and forward position remain defined.

questions.prompt: A planar 2R arm (relative joint angles) has endpoint x = l₁cos q₁ + l₂cos(q₁+q₂), y = l₁sin q₁ + l₂sin(q₁+q₂), and the Jacobian J = ∂(x, y)/∂(q₁, q₂) has J₂₁ = ∂y/∂q₁. With l₁ = l₂ = 1 m and q₁ = q₂ = 0, what is J₂₁ (in m/rad)?
questions.explanation: J₂₁ = ∂y/∂q₁ = l₁cos q₁ + l₂cos(q₁+q₂). At q₁ = q₂ = 0 this is 1 + 1 = 2 m/rad.

questions.prompt: For the planar 2R arm with endpoint y = l₁sin q₁ + l₂sin(q₁+q₂) (relative joint angles), the Jacobian entry J₂₂ = ∂y/∂q₂. With l₁ = l₂ = 1 m and q₁ = q₂ = 0, what is J₂₂ (in m/rad)?
questions.explanation: Only the second term depends on q₂: J₂₂ = l₂cos(q₁+q₂). At q₁ = q₂ = 0 this is 1·1 = 1 m/rad.

questions.prompt: A planar 2R arm with link lengths l₁, l₂ and relative joint angles has endpoint Jacobian J = [[−l₁sin q₁ − l₂sin(q₁+q₂), −l₂sin(q₁+q₂)], [l₁cos q₁ + l₂cos(q₁+q₂), l₂cos(q₁+q₂)]], whose determinant is l₁l₂sin q₂. What is det J at q₂ = 0 (the arm fully stretched)?
questions.explanation: det J = l₁l₂ sin q₂. At q₂ = 0, sin 0 = 0, so det J = 0: the Jacobian is singular and the endpoint cannot move along the arm instantaneously.

questions.prompt: Derive J on a blank page, implement it independently, and compare against directional differences. At a straight arm, propose an endpoint velocity that is impossible instantaneously and explain why. Then move slightly away from singularity and compare the joint rates required for a fixed small task velocity. Record lengths, angles, step size, residual, and assumptions. A short numerical quiz verifies local calculations; unfamiliar transfer still needs separate reviewed evidence.
rubric: Show reasoning and an independent check.
Explain a failure case and an alternative.
